title: Service Assurance Ecosystem Onramp
content:
Purpose:
This is a working plan for a federated "service assurance" onramp — a light-weight program to get three product teams and two infra partners to a baseline SLO posture, observable runbooks, and a repeatable rollout pattern that scales across Redwood. The goal is not a one-time playbook but a small repeatable ‘activation kit’ that teams can consume in 4–6 weeks.

Why this is different: 
- Treat reliability as a product: combine SLOs + UX-level tolerances + automated fallbacks.
- Federated council model: product squads keep ownership; SRE provides guardrails, onboarding, and measurement plumbing.
- Experiment-first: quick pilots with measurable metrics, then iterate.

Scope & constraints:
- In-scope: model-serving endpoints (hosted API + dedicated pools), console routes that surface latency/cost slices, and platform fallback routing.
- Out-of-scope (initial): on-prem private-deploy customer-specific SLAs, billing model changes.
- Constraints: limited SRE headcount for pairings; require one platform engineer for sample traffic shadowing.

Pilot composition (weeks 0–6):
- Teams: Search product team (team A), Chat integrations (team B), Embeddings batch service (team C).
- Platform partners: Serving runtime (infra), Redwood Console (product/observability).
- Success metric for each pilot: defined SLO + telemetry ingest + one verified canary rollback scenario.

High-level timeline (condensed):
- Week 0: kickoff, stakeholder mapping, quick audit of current dashboards and SLO candidates (1 day).
- Week 1: SLO drafting workshop (SRE + product + infra), identify 2–3 candidate SLOs per service.
- Week 2: Instrumentation gaps closed (traces, token-level latency, error classification), Console route created.
- Week 3: Canary config + traffic shadowing run (10% synthetic + 100% shadow), runbook skeleton drafted.
- Week 4: Runbook tabletop + automated alert thresholds wired to escalation channels.
- Week 5: Canary -> gradual rollout with fallback policy enabled; collect metrics.
- Week 6: Post-mortem and onramp packaging (templates + runbook + onboarding checklist).

Roles & responsibilities (working matrix):
- Product Owners (Team A/B/C): finalize user-visible SLOs, provide representative workloads and customer-impact mapping.
- SRE Onramp Lead (Sofia): run workshops, review SLOs, pair on telemetry, author runbook template.
- Infra/Serving-runtime (Marcus): configure traffic shadowing, ensure model variant fallback is available, expose kernel-level metrics if needed.
- Console/Observability (Jordan): create per-route dashboards, short URL to onramp dashboard, ensure sampling config for traces.
- Incident Manager (rotating): run tabletop, validate escalation flow.

Minimum onboarding checklist (deliverable for each service):
1) SLO doc (title, intent, user-impact, measurement window, threshold)
2) Error taxonomy (user-facing errors vs transient infra)
3) Token-level latency histogram + 95th/99th snapshots
4) Dashboard link in Redwood Console + owner list
5) Runbook skeleton (who to call, rollback steps, fallback policy)
6) Canary config and rollback test executed
7) Postmortem template pre-filled with risk/assumptions

Example SLOs (templates for pilots):
- Chat API (interactive): Availability SLO: 99.5% requests with final generation latency < 600ms over 7-day window. Error SLO: <0.1% model-misroute errors (invalid tool calls) per 30 days.
- Search ranker (short queries): Latency SLO: p95 < 120ms for top-5 ranking path over 7-day window. Quality guard: reranker precision on sampled test set must not regress > 2% after model swap.
- Embeddings batch job: Completion SLO: 98% of jobs finish within SLA window (48 hours) per 30-day window. Cost guard: per-embedding unit cost not exceed baseline +10% after quantization change.

Observability & instrumentation notes:
- Signals to collect: per-route token breakdown, model variant label, GPU queue-time, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate, quantization variant tag.
- Tagging convention: service=<name>, route=<route-id>, model_version=<semver-like>, region=<region>, variant=<float16|int8|q4_0>.
- Recommended panels: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate by class, traffic volume, KV cache hit ratio, autoscale gap (demand vs capacity).

Rollout & fallback patterns (practical examples):
- Canary + Shadowing: run candidate model at 5–10% traffic with 100% shadow to verify correctness. Drop to 0% and enable fallback routing if p95 latency exceeds threshold or error spike.
- Graceful degradation: for chat, fallback to smaller model variant with consistent prompt shim to preserve semantics.
- Cost-safety net: if cost-per-token for a route increases >20% vs baseline, auto-throttle non-critical background inference.

Runbook snippet (copyable):
- Trigger: p95 latency > threshold for 15m AND error rate > baseline * 3
- Immediate action: disable new model variant routing (infra: /api/admin/routes/{id}/variants -> set weight 0).
- Short-term mitigation: enable fallback variant, scale dedicated pool by +20% burst if available.
- Pager escalation: oncall -> SRE oncall -> infra owner -> product owner.
- Post-incident: capture token histograms, top-5 failing request examples, compare to shadow run.

Experiment & measurement plan (A/B style):
- For each model swap experiment capture: latency distribution, correctness signal (sampled human eval or automated rerank score), embedding distance drift, cost delta.
- Use a 7-day baseline period and a 7-day experiment window; require statistical signal on both latency and quality or fail fast.

Success criteria (pilot-level):
- Each pilot has a named SLO, dashboard, and runbook linked in Console.
- At least one rollback scenario has been executed end-to-end for each pilot.
- Onramp package (templates + checklist) used by a 4th team with <2 SRE pairing hours required.

Knowledge artifacts to produce:
- Onramp playbook (this doc -> cleaned + linked Confluence page)
- Runbook template + example (markdown + console link)
- SLO starter kit (editable checklist, SLA -> SLO mapping doc)
- Small set of telemetry enrichment PRs for serving-runtime repo (to standardize tags)

Open questions & risks (to discuss in kickoff):
- How tight should user-visible SLOs be for experimental features? (conservative vs aspirational)
- Cost vs reliability tradeoffs: who signs off on cost-safety throttles?
- Observability gaps: which model-internal signals are productively exposed without leaking PII/PI?
- Shielding private-deploy customers from federation changes (out-of-scope but may be impacted).

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Day 0: schedule 45min kickoff with product leads + infra + Console (Sofia to send invite).
- Pre-kickoff homework: product leads send current SLAs, top-3 customer pain points, and representative request traces.
- Infra prework: enable traffic shadowing sandbox and confirm access to one non-prod route.

Meeting agenda (kickoff):
- 0–10m: context, goals, constraints
- 10–25m: each product lead: current state & candidate SLOs (5m each)
- 25–35m: infra & console constraints (shadowing, tagging, dashboards)
- 35–40m: success criteria, timeline, and pairing plan
- 40–45m: next actions & owners

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Keep onboarding minimal: the packaging must be consumable by product engineers with low SRE touch.
- Prototype runbook cells as small scripts (curl commands) to reduce handoffs during incidents.
- Consider a "stability flag" in Console for quick rollbacks.

Draft artifacts to attach after pilot: 
- example-slo-chat-api.md
- runbook-chat-canary-rollback.md
- telemetry-enrichment-pr-template.md

Status: draft — aiming to iterate after kickoff and first pairing.

Unresolved: - Need agreement on cost-thresholds that trigger automated throttles (ownership: finance + product).

Contact: Sofia Patel (sre-oncall@redwood.example)
